column8: Mon 16 Nov: 3e store; the two-step rule (half at approval, all at contract) shows 2031 is an approval-stage figure; row 2 leads, the plan cannot lock a rate anyway (no derivatives, Treasuries held to their end).

Mon 16 Nov: 3e area (4) and Table 3 row 7; answers why not lock the rate in 2031 with a government rule (cover when certain, at the latest at contract; 2031 has no NT$ contract, amount or dates); said as practice, never as an option inside Laura's plan.
Mon 16 Nov: same principle as row 2 (lock the contracted, leave the unconfirmed open), with Waikato's percentages; store only.
Mon 16 Nov: residency's rule, store only; any forward stays outside Laura's plan (derivatives banned), as the row's clash column says.
Mon 16 Nov: 3e one-clause candidate: the NT$ is bought when the bill is known, which is the residency's act, not a change to the plan.
Mon 16 Nov: JCU checklist restates row 2's certainty test; its Table 3 idea is carried by row 43.
Mon 16 Nov: 3e store; locking NT$ before notice to proceed risks a mismatch if the building's timing or size changes, a second reason not to convert in 2031.

Mon 16 Nov: 3b store; a reserve is the recognised alternative to a hedge where hedging is barred; her flexibility is a cushion for three uses, never a natural hedge, and VT is never a Taiwan-dollar hedge.
Mon 16 Nov: 3b or 3e support for row 11; DoD's building example (budgeted FY2017, paid FY2019 at the FY2017 rate) matches the 2031-to-December-2032 lag; one DoD clause at most.

Mon 16 Nov: 3b or 3e aha with row 11; statute wording verified at uscode.house.gov, but the 970m cap is 2779(d)(3)'s, on the Foreign Currency Fluctuations, Defense account (O and M, personnel); the military construction money in (b) is a separate 100m plus 25m appropriation: drop the cap or name the right account. Pot, never hedge.

Mon 16 Nov: 3b or 3e aha: the Defense Department works under Laura's bar (derivatives prohibited) and answers with a pot that buffers, not a hedge; the parallel holds because the half kept is a cushion and never offsets the currency.
Mon 16 Nov: store; the hedging ban has a price (abstract only); with US rates above Taiwan's a forward to buy NT$ costs the interest gap, so never offered as a missed option.
Mon 16 Nov: 3b store; GAO asked a pot to be tested against losses; NUMBERS 8j's test (1.9 times centrally, 93.3% house) is that test, never a sizing of the half kept (CANON A31).
Mon 16 Nov: twin of row 10's purpose; its use line must not say Laura can promise co-sponsors that the move is met elsewhere, since the half kept is promised to no one (CANON A30).
Mon 16 Nov: 3b store; a weaker NT$ leaves the building more NT$ because the contribution is fixed in US dollars; the half kept is for losses only; CBJ figure read via excerpt.
Mon 16 Nov: 3e store, pairs with row 17; the war-graves agency ran its currency pot dry by budgeting at forecast rates (verified at govinfo: balance under 1 million, spending curtailed).

Mon 16 Nov: Table 3 row 7 and 3e area (4); the watch's base is the day's rate, which GAO called nonjudgmental and transparent (verified at source); NUMBERS 8j already uses NT$32.768 on 6 Nov and measures from 2031.
Mon 16 Nov: 3e support: even the US government absorbs post-budget moves and publishes no currency forecast, so the report states a watch, not a forecast.
Mon 16 Nov: 3b or 3d: by default the recipient of a US-dollar gift carries the move; the plain fact behind whose choice (row 42).
Mon 16 Nov: residency toolkit, store only (hold a US-dollar account, convert as bills come).
Mon 16 Nov: 3c or 3d: no currency pad inside the stated range, the cushion outside it; change Laura offers to share it to Laura keeps a pot promised to no one that may help (CANON A30).
Mon 16 Nov: 3d: the currency of the stated figure is decided once and sticks; Laura states US dollars in 2031.
Mon 16 Nov: twin of row 19 across three more funders; its use line overstates, since the half kept is not offered to co-sponsors.
Mon 16 Nov: 3b or 3d: the closest match, a US-dollar gift the recipient converts as needed with a discretionary backstop; generous, not a guarantor, her flexibility promised to no one (IPS l.15).
Mon 16 Nov: store; sample terms a residency could follow (hold safely, report conversions).
Mon 16 Nov: 3d store: transfer in US dollars and let the grantee convert as funds are needed; the half kept is never part of the gift (CANON A30).
Mon 16 Nov: the parallel breaks: Toronto commits so the researcher knows the budget, while Laura's flexibility is promised to no one; drop what Laura's half kept offers the residency.

Mon 16 Nov: 3b, the two options in December 2032; reword the IPS chose the first to the IPS names a stronger Taiwan dollar as one of three uses of her flexibility, promised to no one; otherwise the NT$ budget shrinks.

Mon 16 Nov: the 115,000 against 123,476 gap is the range rule (no interest earned, 0.5% cut, rounding), not a currency margin; use Harvard only as stating less than expected is normal, never as currency cover.
Mon 16 Nov: 3d store only; a scope clause would be the residency's, never in Laura's words.

Mon 16 Nov: store; US dollars held without converting are free, so the residency can convert as bills come; Taiwan regulatory requirements are out of scope (case l.169); rests partly on a press report quoting the CBC.

Mon 16 Nov: the CONFLICTING is resolved: Art. 7 lets the CBC raise Art. 4(1)3's amounts and press release (113) 180 sets 10m and 100m from 1 Nov 2024; the yearly limit is for residents (Art. 3(10)), so the 87-times line does not apply if Laura converts herself; store only.

Mon 16 Nov: verified at law.moj.gov.tw: Art. 4(1)5 is per single conversion against NT$, up to 100,000 dollars, for any non-resident; Art. 6(1)3 lists four purposes and 6(1)4 other necessary remittances, so a gift goes by 6(1)4; case l.13 suggests a non-resident; out of scope, store only.

Mon 16 Nov: re-derived: 115,000 x 2 years x 2.76 to 3.68 points = 6,348 to 8,464 (compounded 6,544 to 8,686), 55-74% of 8j's 11,500; not in NUMBERS, so Keel arithmetic and store only; say half to three-quarters, never about half; clash holds (IPS l.17 two reasons, CANON A8, A34; derivatives banned).
Mon 16 Nov: reproduced exactly on the repo mirror (505 windows; 5.7, 13.0 and 10.1%; 7.3% and 22.2%); the residency's conversion choice, store only.
Mon 16 Nov: checked on the mirror (median 0.15% and 0.0%; 12.8% in eight months, 19.4% over 26); a later conversion date is a bet, which echoes Trading Note 3 without restating it.
Mon 16 Nov: 3e check: 8q's episodes hold on the mirror (7.24%, Jan-Jun 2008 6.55%, 16.31%); name the monthly basis when quoted.
Mon 16 Nov: 3b or 3d: the currency a gift is written in decides who carries the move; Fulbright Taiwan pays in NT$ and carries it, Laura writes US dollars.
Mon 16 Nov: store; Taiwan arts grants fix each cost in the currency it is spent in.
Mon 16 Nov: twin of Cloud Gate's US-dollar gift: Taiwan's arts world is used to gifts stated in US dollars.
Mon 16 Nov: 3d colour, store only; a US gift for a Taiwan building stated in US dollars (1963, nominal, no conversion detail).

Mon 16 Nov: 3e or 3d clause answering Q10b's gap (who converts); reword the IPS: yes, from her flexibility to the IPS names a stronger Taiwan dollar as one of three uses of her flexibility, promised to no one (CANON A30-A31).
Mon 16 Nov: Table 3 row 7: fits the printed 10% stronger than in 2031 and 8j's measure from the meetings; the contract share goes to 3e prose if the table is full.

Mon 16 Nov: 3e conceit turn candidate extending CONCEIT's Taiwan dollar line (the ink holds, what it buys changes); NT$3.77m checks with 8j; one turn per part, and her flexibility stands behind it never as a promise.
Mon 16 Nov: store; release timing is card Q24's suggestion, and the IPS sets none.
